chapter: Big band, Chicago players, recordings and gospel
title: Sitters-in: Strayhorn, Charlie Parker and Clark Terry
summary: Everyone sat in at the DeLisa; Billy Strayhorn slept it off under the piano and Clark Terry came from Great Lakes Navy.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Would guys come out and sit in?
Right, right, see. We got to hear everybody, because that was the meeting place. And God bless the dead, when Sweet Pea --

Billy, uh-huh, with Duke, he would make that his home. And then he'd get drunk we'd put him under the piano and let him sleep it off, because we'd be there til 5:00 the next morning. And Parker, Charlie Parker, he used to come out quite often, when he was in town, when he was working at the Rum Boogie. Yeah.
So -- Clark Terry, they were in the Navy at the time, and he used to come out, and they used to -- I don't know how those sailors did it. They were --
Great Lakes, they would take their leave and then get back just in time to go -- up all night long, yeah, really something.
Yeah. And there weren't very good roads, then.
On, no,no, no, right, right. That was really --
Had to be close to 60 miles.
